title: Minimum Path Sum
summary: Determine the path with the least sum from the top-left corner to the bottom-right corner in a m x n grid of non-negative numbers, allowing only downward or rightward movements.
statement: Determine the path with the least sum from the top-left corner to the bottom-right corner in a m x n grid of non-negative numbers, allowing only downward or rightward movements.
constraints: A rectangular 1–200 by 1–200 grid has cell values between 0 and 200.
Move only right or down. Include both the starting and destination cell values in the total.
hints: A cheapest route to a cell must use a cheapest route to one of its two predecessors.
Add the current cell cost to the smaller reachable predecessor total.
Update a row array left to right; the old same-column value comes from above and the new previous-column value comes from the left.
Equivalently, recursively minimize the right/down continuation and memoize coordinates; boundaries must be unreachable, not free.
editorial: The DP entry for a cell is its value plus the smaller cost from above or left. A single row array retains the previous row until each entry is replaced; initialize only the virtual predecessor of the starting cell to zero and other unreachable states to infinity. This includes both endpoints and handles zero costs correctly. The oracle enumerates complete routes and directly sums their cells.

tests.explanation: Following right, right, down, down visits 1+3+1+1+1=7, the minimum.
The cheapest route visits 1,2,3,6 for a total of 12.
